newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Rabobank, Robeco finalise asset deal.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Rabobank, Robeco finalise asset deal.

text.p: Dutch cooperative Rabobank and the Robeco group of investment funds said on Tuesday they had finalised Rabobank's takeover of 50 percent of Robeco's management company which was announced last June.
The management unit will be renamed Robeco Group NV.
"Rabobank now owns 50 percent of the shares in Robeco Group NV, the new management company," they said in a joint statement.

In line with previous announcements, Rabo will pay 530 million guilders for the first tranche of the management group. Robeco said this implied a book profit of 350 million guilders, which will all be paid to its 16 investment funds.
The 350 million guilders will raise the net asset value per share of the 16 funds, which will also positively affect their prices on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, Robeco said.
The group's four largest investment funds, Robeco, Rolinco, Rorento and Rodamco, each receive 44.9 million guilders out of the book profit.
Nettorente Fund, Florente Fund and Divirente Fund get payments of 41.5 million, 41.2 million and 35.7 million guilders respectively. All the smaller mutual funds receive 5.8 million guilders each.
Rabobank has the option to acquire the remaining half of the new holding Robeco Group NV at a price of 585 million guilders during a period of at least four years.
As long as Rabobank has not acquired the remaining half of Robeco Group, the investment funds concerned will jointly receive a cumulative preferred dividend of 45 million guilders per year.
"The remaining profit will go to Rabobank," the joint statement said.
Within Robeco Group NV, all asset management activities -- except in the area of property - have been combined into two operating companies, Robeco Nederland BV and Robeco International BV.

RoProperty Services BV will be the management company for property activities and will keep real estate investment fund Rodamco as its main client. But in the new set-up RoProperty is no longer a wholly owned subsidiary of Robeco Group.
In the new construction, which was chosen to clear legal hurdles in the U.S., Robeco Group will only own five percent of RoProperty.
Rodamco will hold 60 percent of RoProperty and unidentified third parties the remaining 35 percent.

Rabobank and Robeco began cooperating in the field of investments in 1990, but they decided to tighten the cooperation because the financial services industry is rapidly becoming more international and new distribution methods were being launched.
Robeco said teaming up with a triple-A bank would also enable it to finance its necessary international expansion.
The new cooperation also anticipates the setting up of the Economic and Monetary Union in Europe, the statement said.
